title: GST Time, Value and Place of Supply

content.overview: Time of supply fixes when GST is payable. Value is determined under section 15, generally the transaction value if price is the sole consideration and the parties are not related. Place of supply decides whether the supply is intra-State or inter-State and which Act applies. A wrong time, value or place changes the return, the rate application or the statute. Each has its own section.
content.glance: GST Time, Value and Place of Supply. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Fix time, then value, then place. Do not use one date for all three.

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

enhancement.definition: Time of supply fixes when GST is payable. Value is determined under section 15, generally the transaction value if price is the sole consideration and the parties are not related. Place of supply decides whether the supply is intra-State or inter-State and which Act applies.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: A wrong time, value or place changes the return, the rate application or the statute. Each has its own section.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: CGST Act, 2017, sections 12, 13 and 15; IGST Act, 2017, sections 10 to 13.
essentialIngredients: Time of supply for goods or services
Transaction value unless section 15 displaces it
Place of supply under the IGST rules
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Sections 12 and 13 set time of supply by invoice date, payment date and the enacted residuary dates. Section 15 uses transaction value where the statutory conditions hold, and adds specified amounts such as taxes other than GST, supplier obligations, incidental expenses and interest for late payment, while excluding discounts recorded as the section requires. Place of supply for goods depends on movement and delivery. Place of supply for services depends on the enacted category, with a residuary rule.
examples: An invoice is issued before delivery and payment.
Time of supply follows the section 12 dates, not the contract date alone.
A related-party price is not automatically transaction value.
A service supplied to a registered person is located by the place-of-supply section, not by the invoice heading.
